text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Baltic Assambly session took place in Riga over the weekend, calling for movement towards Western structures and cooperation. An Estonian proposal for the abolition of capital punishment was withdrawn due to lack of support.
- Rescue Department bought fire engines and other equipment with funds allocated for construction of a training facility.
- The newspaper published an interview with Juhan Simonson, long-time chairman of the Estonian National Committee in the USA, on his past and the activities of the committee.
- Estonia beat Belarus 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier on Saturday, taking revenge for defeat in Minsk on August 31.
- The national theatre festival ended in Tartu and the jury awarded 10 equal prizes to actors and directors.
- Union Bank shareholders authorised the board to issue two million preference shares as an incentive to the staff.
- Estonian historian Juhan Maiste received the Baltic Assembly science awards on Saturday.
- The police warns that credit card forgeries are spreading in Estonia, particularly in restaurants.
- Estonian export increased in August by 16.5 percent and import decreased by 1 percent.
- Italian businessman Ernesto Preatoni brought a delegation of 126 Italian investors to Estonia; the Italians expressed approval at Estonian taxing system and the absence of excessive state control.
